chapter: Technique and life on the road (repeated passages)
title: Being stranded at his first out-of-town job in Madison
summary: He tells again how he was fired in Madison for not reading after paying fifteen dollars a week for a trombone, and saved himself with a piano gig.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: I suppose you could say we were kinda halfway stranded in a couple of places. But always we managed to get out of it. On my first job I was stranded. But I got a little gig playing the piano. I couldn't play too well, but I could sing, and you know, mess around with it. The drummer wanted a piano player, and couldn't find many. And I was stranded at the time.

That was my first job out of town. I went to Madison, Wisconsin from Columbus, Ohio. And the guy fired me because I couldn't read, all of a sudden... I bought a horn from one of the players in the band; I bought a horn from him -- and I paid him fifteen dollars a week for it. He wanted sixty dollars for it. I should have known then, four weeks, DING. And I was only getting thirty-five dollars a week. Dig? And my room and board cost me close to $15, so that left me with a five. You know? So the end of this four weeks, they told me, says... The boss told me he had found a guy that could read, and so "we don't need you any more." Without any notice, you know?

So I only had five dollars, heh-heh, after I paid him and paid my rent. Now, I had to get back to Columbus, Ohio. I don't know how I could do it, so... It happened that night, this guy wanted a piano player, and so I got that
gig. And we got a tip on it even! So that made me, you know, able to get away.
